title: Constant shrink and error-driven correction after a short causal filter
summary: Inputs first pass through a short causal filter over the last four embeddings. The filtered vector gives a unit-length address, a content and a step size. The square store is shrunk by one learned constant per layer and then corrected toward the content along the address by the misprediction of the shrunk store.
core_idea: Filter the last four inputs causally, then shrink a square store by a learned constant and correct it along the new address by the prediction error of the new content.

state.name: S
state.meaning: Square store from addresses to contents; shrunk by the constant alpha and corrected at every symbol.

state.name: F
state.meaning: The last four input embeddings, used by the causal filter.

update.name: filter
update.plain: v_t = sum over j = 0..3 of w_j * e_(t-j), elementwise filter weights w_j, with e_t = E[x_t]

update.name: projections
update.latex: k_t = \frac{W_k v_t}{\lVert W_k v_t \rVert},\; u_t = W_u v_t,\; \beta_t = \sigma(w_\beta^{\top} v_t)
update.plain: k_t = W_k v_t normalized to unit length; u_t = W_u v_t; beta_t = sigmoid(w_beta . v_t)

update.name: correction
update.plain: S_t = alpha S_(t-1) + beta_t * outer(u_t - alpha S_(t-1) k_t, k_t), with alpha in (0, 1] one learned constant (decay)

readout.name: read
readout.plain: y_t = S_t times the unit-length probe W_q v_t / norm; next symbol scores O y_t

learning.description: Every matrix and offset is learned by gradient descent on the cross-entropy of the next symbol over a training corpus, with backpropagation through the whole sequence.
learning.few_shot_argument: No structure for few examples; about 2400 training sequences are needed for recall of 4 pairs.

complexity.constants_notes: A four-tap filter, three projections, one misprediction product, one rank-one correction and one read per symbol; the store is d^2 numbers plus the 4 d buffer.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Gradient descent with no structure for few examples.

prediction.statement: From random weights, 2400 training sequences of 4 pairs over 16 symbols give recall accuracy 0.99.

capabilities.prediction: Exact with hand-set orthonormal addresses, alpha = 1 and beta = 1 when K <= d.
The filter lets an address depend on the previous symbol, so a pair written as two adjacent symbols is bound with no extra layer.

known_relatives.name: not assessed
known_relatives.relation: This card does not compare its mechanism with others.
known_relatives.claimed_difference: No difference from earlier work is claimed.

falsifiers: With alpha = beta = 1 and orthonormal addresses, rewriting an address leaves a mixture of contents.
The counted operations grow faster than linearly in n at fixed d and V.

toy_example.description: One address written twice with alpha = 0.9 and beta = 1, then read.
toy_example.python:
import json
a = 0.9
S = [[0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0]]
def step(S, k, u):
    pred = [a * (S[i][0] * k[0] + S[i][1] * k[1]) for i in range(2)]
    return [[a * S[i][j] + (u[i] - pred[i]) * k[j] for j in range(2)] for i in range(2)]
S = step(S, [1.0, 0.0], [1.0, 1.0])
S = step(S, [0.0, 1.0], [2.0, 0.0])
S = step(S, [1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 3.0])
print(json.dumps({"read_first": [round(S[0][0], 6), round(S[1][0], 6)], "read_second": [round(S[0][1], 6), round(S[1][1], 6)]}))
